title: Hybrid allocation weave: predictive slot shepherding and opportunistic microdefrag
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal allocation lead to increased GPU memory usage and higher tail latency under continuous-batching workloads. Goal: implement a hybrid allocation strategy that combines low-fragmentation placement hints, live slot shepherding for long-lived KV entries, and opportunistic micro-defragmentation windows to reduce memory waste while preserving latency SLOs. Target: reduce effective KV memory footprint by 18-28% on typical chat/beam workloads and eliminate tail latency regressions caused by full-scan compaction during peak.

Scope: allocator-level changes, runtime scheduling hooks (to schedule micro-defrag in slack windows), telemetry additions for per-slot age/heat, rollout as runtime-1.24 canary, and dashboard to track fragmentation heatmap + memory reclaimed. Not in scope: changing model formats, on-disk checkpoints, or customer-visible API changes.

High-level approach:
1) Allocation weave: introduce a lightweight placement hint layer above existing slab allocator. Hints annotate allocation intents (transient, sticky, high-entropy) so similar lifetime entries are colocated to reduce internal fragmentation. Hints are derived from request traces (prefix lengths, repetition rate, KV lifetime heuristics) and reinforced by evictions.
2) Slot shepherding: mark long-lived KV slots as "shepherded" and bias them to dedicated micro-stripes. When shepherded slots are cold but stable, use in-place compaction-friendly chaining instead of immediate relocation.
3) Opportunistic micro-defrag: rather than large background compactions, run short defrag passes aligned to GPU idle slices (e.g., during model reloads, short inter-batch gaps). Micro-pass constraints: limited to N ms or M MB reclaimed per pass, preemptible, and observable.
4) Allocation backpressure and admission: when fragmentation exceeds threshold, throttle large batch admissions or divert to a fallback lower-memory model variant. This integrates with smart routing to avoid noisy neighbours.

Instrumentation and observability:
- New metrics: per-pool fragmentation_ratio, per-stripe shepherded_fraction, microdefrag_reclaimed_bytes, microdefrag_pass_duration_ms, eviction_age_histogram.
- Heatmap: live stripe heatmap of allocation density and age percentiles to drive automated hint tuning.
- Traces: attach allocation hint provenance to request traces for debugging.

Benchmarks and acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic workload 1 (multi-turn chat, bursty prefixes): 20% reduction in KV memory usage vs baseline, 99th percentile latency within 5%
- Production replay (last 7d): reduce total-live-kv bytes by at least 15% and reduce incidence of emergency full compactions to near-zero
- Microdefrag overhead under 2% tail-latency impact during canary windows

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Why hints vs aggressive compaction: aggressive compaction yields bigger wins but causes latency spikes. Hints are low-risk and guide allocation without immediate disruptive movement.
- Shepherding increases risk of hot slow-to-evict slots; mitigated via periodic review and adaptive un-shepherd thresholds.
- Micro-defrag pass sizing is conservative to avoid destabilizing GPU utilization.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement allocator hint layer behind a runtime flag, collect heatmap + metrics in internal canary (dev cluster).
2) Enable shepherding in dev, observe eviction curves for 48 hours.
3) Run micro-defrag scheduled in low-util windows in preprod for 72 hours.
4) Canary in 5% of production trafﬁc with automatic rollback if key metrics (99p latency, OOMs) regress.
5) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with monitoring alerts.

Backward compatibility and fail-safe:
- All features are opt-in flags. If micro-defrag causes regressions it can be disabled at runtime. Allocation hints degrade gracefully to default slab behavior when disabled.

Security & compliance notes:
- No customer data extracted; hints are derived from token-length and access patterns only. Feature flagged for private deployments until compliance review for VPC metrics is complete.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Shepherding creates fragmentation by creating small stranded islands. Mitigation: periodic global reclamation window during low-traffic and harnessed by microdefrag metrics to detect islands.
- Risk: Incorrect heuristics cause thrashing. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, telemetry for quick rollback, and staged A/B experiments.
comments: 2026-02-02 - Marco Chen: Spike complete. Implemented hint header on allocation API and collected initial heatmaps on dev-gpu-4. Observed clear separation between transient and sticky footprints. Next: implement shepherding lanes.

2026-02-18 - Asha Patel: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to limit microdefrag to 50ms window and 4MB reclaimed per pass initially. Ops requested explicit metric for microdefrag_preemptions.

2026-02-25 - Review feedback from Priya Rao (SRE): add admission control hook to routing layer to prevent canary from amplifying fragmentation. Action: add dependency to ENG-422101 (routing-admission-hooks).

2026-03-03 - Marco Chen: Prototype shepherding lanes merged to branch: github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/5467. Benchmark results: 17% avg KV reduction on chat-replay with negligible 95p latency change.
2026-03-09 - QA: Preprod run 48h. One observed microdefrag pass caused 3% CPU spike on host; adjusted scheduling to align with model epoch boundaries. No OOMs or regressions recorded.
